claims.text: A CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy-alloy coating with minor elemental substitutions can form a diffusion-mediated interface with a copper substrate.
The diffusion-mediated interface will improve interfacial adhesion to copper.
The tailored CoCrFeNi-based coating will enhance the wear resistance of the copper substrate.
Minor elemental additions can adjust the coating's chemical affinity for copper.
Minor elemental additions can adjust the coating's coefficient of thermal expansion to better match copper.
Bare copper requires a protective coating to provide high wear resistance.
An interfacial diffusion layer promotes chemical bonding between the HEA coating and copper.
An interfacial diffusion layer mitigates coefficient-of-thermal-expansion mismatch between the HEA coating and copper.
Minor substitutions alter the chemical potential of the CoCrFeNi-based alloy.
Minor substitutions alter the thermal-expansion properties of the CoCrFeNi-based alloy.
Changes in chemical potential and thermal expansion facilitate diffusion-layer formation and bonding at the copper interface.
The elemental tailoring will maintain the inherent high wear resistance of the high-entropy alloy.
The tailored coating will provide greater wear resistance than unprotected copper.
The tailored coating will provide greater wear resistance than an untailored CoCrFeNi-based coating.
The tailored coating will provide greater interfacial adhesion than an untailored CoCrFeNi-based coating.
The proposed benefits may be limited to moderate temperature fluctuations and wear conditions.
Extreme service conditions may require further compositional tuning.
